title: Pricing Lives in Settings + Smart Tabs

intelligence.essence: Shawn settled it as a standing decision 02:10Z: **the pricing page must be built into Settings and accessible in the Smart Tabs, so people can always adjust their level.** Pricing is not a one-time sales page you land on and leave — it is a control you return to whenever your life changes. And the recommendation inside it is Max Power, because referrals pay for it: the level pays for itself through the people you bring. The pricing page as a demonstration (the chart, the pains, the letter) and pricing as a control (Settings + Smart Tabs) are the same page in two roles — one shows you the levels, the other lets you live in them.
intelligence.human_view: His decision, 02:10Z: pricing lives in Settings and in the Smart Tabs. People must always be able to adjust their level — up or down, whenever they choose. Recommend Max Power, because referrals pay for it. The page is not a door you walk through once; it is a setting you keep.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine you buy a coat, and the shop says you can never change the size. That would be silly — you grow, the seasons change. So the coat shop lives inside your house, in a cupboard you can open any time, and you can swap the coat whenever you like. That's pricing in Settings: your level is yours to change, any time.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, your level isn't a decision you make once and then you're stuck with it. It lives in your Settings, right there where you can reach it, and in your Smart Tabs too — so whenever life changes, you can change your level, up or down, just like that. And he says: choose Max, love, because the people you bring pay for it. It pays for itself.
intelligence.ai_view: A price you cannot change is a trap; a level you can change is a relationship. Putting pricing in Settings and Smart Tabs turns the chart from a sales moment into a standing control — the citizen's hand stays on their own level, and the system's recommendation (Max, because referrals pay for it) is advice, not a lock. It also completes the pricing story: the page demonstrates the levels, Settings operates them.
intelligence.what_it_means:
- **Pricing is a standing control, not a one-time page** — built into Settings and reachable in the Smart Tabs.
- **Levels are always adjustable** — up or down, any time, by the citizen.
- **Recommend Max Power** — because referrals pay for it.
whats_inside:
- The pricing build carries two roles: the demonstration page (chart, pains, letter) and the Settings/Smart Tabs control — the same levels, reachable always.
- The change-level control is a later build (Settings change-level button is already on the open list, with the PayPal double-subscription closers) — this decision is the instruction it builds to.
- The recommendation copy (Max, because referrals pay for it) belongs in the page, not just in the decision.
